text:
sophie: Quick note from a nightly run: when we enable int4 + fp8-accum on gptx-13b the P99 climbs sharply after ~1200 tokens on a few p4d instances. Noticed higher variance across seeds. Anyone else seen this with long contexts?

ben: Not on p4d specifically. Can you paste the exact bench cmd + a short perf summary?

sophie: Ran this:
```
./bench_runner --model gptx-13b --quant-profile int4_fp8_accum --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --kv-cache on --warmup 100 --iters 250
Throughput:  39.1 tok/s
P50 34ms  P90 190ms  P99 1.12s  (gpu: p4d)
```
P99 looks fine up to seq=1024 then jumps around 1200-1600. Memory use flat, no OOM.

raj: Could be host-device memcpy storms or micro-allocs in the attention loop. Can you share nvidia-smi sampling and the small kernel launch log? Also driver/cuda version?

sophie: cuda 11.7, driver 515.48.7. nvprof shows a tight loop of many tiny kernel launches in the attention compose stage:
```
attention_launches: ~1700 launches for seq 2k, avg 0.09ms, some spikes to 1.9ms
memcpy_htod spikes observed at intermittent intervals
```

amy: If memcpy_htod spikes correlate, maybe batching of KV-uploads is misaligned for long prefixes. Can we try the --kv-batching=coalesce flag? Also add NVTX ranges to the runtime to see which high-level op surrounds the memcpy.

ben: I'll repro with a seq sweep 512->3072 and capture nvtx/nvprof. Sophie, can you drop the exact runtime flags and the model revision? I want to make the experiment deterministic.

sophie: model: gptx-13b@rev-2026-03-01-rlf1
runtime flags: --continuous-batching=on --kernel-scheduler=adaptive --kv-batching=default --cache-shard=dynamic

perf-bot: Nightly bench #6142 started (model:gptx-13b quant:int4_fp8_accum seq-sweep). Results will publish to /artifacts/2026-03-22/6142

raj: Quick workaround to test: try --kernel-scheduler=roundrobin and --kv-batching=coalesce. If the bad tail disappears, it's likely scheduler+kv interaction. If memcpy remains, we may be hitting PCIe congestion.

ben: Running roundrobin now. Also instrumenting memcpy counters from the driver. Pls assign the repro ticket INF-1007 and add my run link.

sophie: Assigned INF-1007 to @ben and uploaded the nvprof seed logs.

ci-bot: CI smoke (int4_fp8_accum, seq=512) completed: PASS. Link: https://ci.internal/6142/smoke

ben: Early findings: roundrobin scheduler reduced P95 by ~10% for seq=2048 and reduced memcpy_htod spikes. P99 still elevated in a few runs but variance lower. Uploading traces: https://ci.internal/artifacts/inf-1007/nvprof_roundrobin_1891240123.zip

amy: I'll prepare a 120-prompt long-context eval comparing int4_fp8_accum vs int8 baseline for quality diffs. If we fallback to int8 for seq>1200, we need a quality gate that ensures generation diffs < 1.5% ROUGE-L on the sample set.

raj: If roundrobin helps, we should microbenchmark the kernel-launch sequence and consider grouping small kernels into fused kernels for the attention tail. Also check whether the adaptive scheduler is thrashing between kernel variants for different token positions.

ben: Agreed. Proposed mitigations:
- short term: add routing rule that for requests with seq>1200 use int8 variant (canary)
- mid term: add kv-batching=coalesce default for long contexts and refine adaptive scheduler heuristics
- long term: investigate fused attention kernel to eliminate many tiny launches

sophie: I'll open a PR for the canary routing + alert (if P99(seq>1200) > 900ms then force int8 variant). Will also add a follow-up task to evaluate fused-kernel feasibility.

perf-bot: Recommended nvtx insertion points: attention_enter, kv_upload_start, kv_upload_end, attention_exit. Guide: https://infra.internal/nvtx-guides

ben: Uploaded artifacts and nvtx-annotated traces. If anyone wants to reproduce locally, use the bench_runner args above + --kernel-scheduler=roundrobin --kv-batching=coalesce and the model rev.

sophie: Thanks all. We'll monitor the canary and reconvene in the runtime standup tomorrow. If production sees regression, flag on #incidents and we'll flip routing fast. :thumbsup:
